chapter_title: The Apostle is asked: Why when you drew every thing in the Picture (- Book), did you not draw the Purification of the Catechumens who shall be cleansed by Transmigration?
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by hagiographic dialogue scaffolding and institutional categories (catechumen/elect), with a formulaic closing and strong pastoral drift in the second half. The content about post-mortem judgment/gehenna/transmigration is presented entirely through catechetical/institutional framing rather than impersonal systematic cosmological exposition; no recoverable pre-compilation core teaching layer can be cleanly extracted here.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Scene-setting dialogue frame (“Once again…”, catechumen addresses “our enlightener”). No impersonal cosmological exposition.
Institutional/ethical-eschatological catechesis (righteous vs sinner; Judge; dispenser of justice; gehenna). Not presented as systematic cosmological mechanics; functions as didactic reassurance.

Continues catechumen’s institutional concern and devotional language (“path of the catechumen”, ‘rest for ever’, desire to ‘see … face to face’). The register is paraenetic/catechetical rather than structural cosmology.

Dialogue attribution (“Then speaks the enlightener…”) marks compilation frame; although it contains an explanation, it is embedded in the frame and oriented to catechumen/elect institutional categories.

Explicit institutional seam-content: ‘middle way of the purification of the catechumen’ contrasted with elect; practical rationale about multiple places. This reads as church-catechesis about catechumen status, not an older systematic mapping.
Formulaic closing response of the catechumen (“heard… persuaded… kept silent”)—typical hagiographic/editorial closure.
